EPFL Packathon, 2026

The maintainers of the Sphere Packing project are excited to announce an in-person "Packathon" at EPFL from 23 to 27 November at the Bernoulli Centre at EPFL, Switzerland. The objective of the Packathon will be for participants to work on the project in dedicated focus-groups led by project maintainers, similar to the FLT workshop that took place in London earlier this year.

We currently have in mind the following working groups:

  1. Contour integration - We are very interested in proving general versions of the Cauchy-Goursat Theorem, the Residue Theorem, and other important theorems concerning contour integration. The hope would be to get general results for Mathlib and specific results for the sphere packing project.
  2. Analytic continuation - A certain integral formula for the magic function needs to be extended by analytic continuation, which requires some work.
  3. Mathlib Upstreaming - This may require redesigning some definitions and API.
  4. Metaprogramming - One specific goal would be to try and develop a tactic for integral computations, which can sometimes be tedious to do in Lean.
  5. SphereCeti - An experiment in autoformalisation. SphereCeti is intended to be to the sphere packing project what Tau Ceti currently is to Mathlib.
  6. Target practice - Before the workshop we will add a collection of self-contained target statements to the repository. Pick one and prove it! (More beginner-friendly)

This list is indicative, and groups may be merged or subdivided based on interest. New groups may also be added, and we welcome suggestions. More detailed descriptions are on the workshop website.

Participation

Participation will be primarily in-person. Anyone interested in participating should fill out this application form by 2026-10-30T23:59:00+01:00 (30 October, 23:59 CET). We will fund accommodation for all participants. Travel funding will be handled case by case. We will also support remote participation to some degree (details TBA), but we would prioritise in-person participation.

The Packathon is a working week, not a Lean tutorial. We expect most participants to have some formalisation experience. We will try and keep a few goals open to Lean beginners, especially as part of the target practice working group, but we would require individuals with very limited Lean background to at least be familiar with the underlying mathematics.

Format

The week will open with an introductory lecture on Monday 23 November by Chris Birkbeck, Sidharth Hariharan and Seewoo Lee, outlining the non-formal and formal aspects of the argument and providing context for important design choices made in the project, followed by another on Tuesday by Maryna Viazovska offering deeper insights into the underlying mathematics. There may be some talks from Wednesday to Friday, but the priority will be the working groups, and most of each day will be spent working in them. We will endeavour to livestream the talks.

Before the workshop, we will add precisely stated targets to the repository and update the blueprint and project dashboard so that groups can start right away.

More details, including the schedule and travel information, are on the workshop website.

We look forward to seeing you in Lausanne!

-- @Chris Birkbeck, @Cameron Freer, @Sidharth Hariharan, @Seewoo Lee and @Maryna Viazovska
